The full-day cruise begins at the port of Punta Bandera, approximately 47 km from El Calafate. The boat travels through the northern part of Lake Argentino, passing through Boca del Diablo toward the Upsala Channel among icebergs that have broken away from the glacier.

The route then continues through the Spegazzini Channel. Along the way, you can see the Seco, Spegazzini, Heim Sur and Peineta glaciers. After landing at the Spegazzini base, there is a walk of around 300 meters along a forest trail to a refuge with viewpoints and themed stops. This is a longer glacier cruise than the included "Water Safari": instead of a single approach to Perito Moreno, it visits several glaciers and includes a separate landing.

After the excursion, return to Puerto Bandera and transfer to the hotel.

The excursion then continues through the impressive Patagonian landscapes of Sofia Lagoon, the Prat Massif, Lake Porteño, Cerro Mesa and Lake Toro.

There is a stop at the Grey viewpoint before the route continues to the village of Río Serrano. Next comes a walk along Lake Grey through a lenga forest. On the lake shore, you may see icebergs that have broken off the glacier and are drifting in the water. Lunch is at a local restaurant.

After lunch, visit a viewpoint overlooking Lake Pehoé and the Salto Grande waterfall. From here, a pleasant walk leads to the 18-meter-high waterfall. The route then visits viewpoints over Lake Nordenskjöld, Laguna Amarga and Mirador Sarmiento.

Return to Puerto Natales, arriving at around 18:45.

## Landscapes of Torres del Paine

Torres del Paine is recognizable by its tall rock formations rising above lakes and open valleys. The Paine Massif, forested areas and wide spaces under the southern sky sit side by side within the park. The color of the water and the visibility of the peaks change with the clouds: the same landscape can look entirely different throughout the day.

Among the park's best-known sights are the Torres towers and the Cuernos peaks. These are different parts of the massif, each with its own silhouette. They illustrate the beauty of the area, although the specific views and stops depend on the excursion route. A group tour lets you explore the park alongside other travelers.

Torres del Paine is ideal for those who enjoy mountain panoramas and want to see Chilean Patagonia. Bring layers, wind protection and comfortable shoes. Walking conditions depend on the weather and itinerary; longer treks and the hike to the base of the towers are arranged as separate options.

## Tortuga Bay

It is among the 25 best beaches in the world. We will walk for approximately 45 minutes to reach the beach. This roughly 2 km stretch of white sand, formed from fish bones and white coral, is considered a sanctuary for iguanas, sea turtles and other species. Visitors can swim and enjoy activities such as bathing and beach games.

## Highlands with Tortoises

This is the natural habitat of around 8,000 giant tortoises from Santa Cruz Island. They prefer the island's highlands, where the climate is cooler and wetter, and where they find more food and rainwater.

## Lava Tunnels and Twin Craters

Lava tunnels are magnificent geological formations through which hot lava once flowed. We will explore the tunnels from inside, accompanied by a naturalist.

The Twin Craters are a pair of sinkholes on opposite sides of the road, hence their name. Here we have the opportunity to see the famous forest of Scalesia, a plant endemic to the Galápagos Islands, and one of the finches' favorite habitats. The main activities are walking, photography and video recording; sports shoes are recommended.
